mainTopic: Where a כתם makes a woman טמאה, and שמואל's rule that she must feel the blood (הרגשה)
overview: The משנה gives a simple test for a כתם (blood stain): could blood from בית התורפה have reached the spot where it was found? It applies this test to her body, her legs and feet, her robe and sleeve, and finally to a robe she sleeps under and a kerchief, where a stain anywhere counts. The גמרא opens with שמואל's rule: a woman is טמאה only if she feels the blood leave her body. He learns this from the word ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״, and the גמרא shows that this one word can teach several laws at once. Next the גמרא tests שמואל against three sources: blood while urinating, a בדיקה cloth under the pillow, and blood found after relations. Each time it answers that she did feel something, but the feeling could have had another cause. A ברייתא about three doubtful cases is answered the same way: 'follow the majority' means she usually feels it when she bleeds. Along the way, the גמרא explains how a doubtful stain can be טמא on her body but טהור on her garment, by setting the case in a butchers' market or after she jumped. Finally, stain cases themselves seem to make her טמאה without any feeling. רב ירמיה מדפתי answers that שמואל agrees she is טמאה, and his explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A stain on her body: near the opening or not
steps.stepSummary: A כתם on her flesh near בית התורפה makes her טמאה. Away from it, she is טהורה. A stain on her heel or the tip of her big toe still makes her טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who finds a stain on her skin across from the opening of her body is impure. If it is not across from that opening, she is pure. If it is on her heel or on the tip of her big toe, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the basic rule for a כתם found on a woman's body. What matters is whether it is near בית התורפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether blood from inside her body could have reached that spot. Near בית התורפה it could, so we worry it is menstrual blood and she is טמאה. The heel and big toe are far away, yet she is still טמאה, because blood can reach those places too.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on the body or on clothing, as opposed to blood she felt coming out
The body opening where menstrual blood comes out
Across from, opposite, in line with

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the rule is only 'close to the opening means טמאה.' The heel and toe are far away, yet she is still טמאה. The real test is whether blood could reach the spot, not just how close it is.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A woman who sees a stain on her flesh
across from her vagina is impure,
and if not across from her vagina, she is pure.

phrases.aramaic: עַל עֲקֵבָהּ וְעַל רֹאשׁ גּוּדָלָהּ — טְמֵאָה.
phrases.english: On her heel or on the tip of her big toe, she is impure.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כתם on the body makes her טמאה only where blood from בית התורפה could reach: across from the opening, and also on the heel and tip of the big toe.

steps.title: A stain on her legs or feet: inside, outside, or sides
steps.stepSummary: On her leg or foot, a stain on the inner side makes her טמאה. A stain on the outer side, or on the front or back sides, leaves her טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the stain is on her leg or on her feet: on the inner side she is impure, on the outer side she is pure. On the sides, this way or that way, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה uses the same test for the legs and feet. It splits each one into inner side, outer side, and the two other sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inner side faces the body, so blood could run down there, and she is טמאה. The outer side and the front and back sides are not in the path of the blood, so she is טהורה.

keyTerms.meaning: On the inner side / on the outer side
From here and from there, meaning both sides

phrases.english: On her leg or on her feet:
on the inner side she is impure, on the outer side she is pure,
and on the sides, from here and from there, she is pure.
phrases.notes: The two 'sides' are the front and the back of the leg or foot, the parts that are neither inner nor outer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same 'could blood reach here?' test to more parts of the body.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On legs and feet, only the inner side makes her טמאה. The outer side and the other sides leave her טהורה.

steps.title: A stain on her robe or its sleeve
steps.stepSummary: On her חלוק, a stain below the belt makes her טמאה and above the belt she is טהורה. On the sleeve, it depends on whether that part of the sleeve can reach across from בית התורפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she saw a stain on her robe from the belt and down, she is impure. From the belt and up, she is pure. If she saw it on the sleeve of the robe: if it reaches across from the opening, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from her body to her clothing and uses the same test. It looks at the robe first, then the sleeve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Below the belt the robe hangs where blood could reach, so she is טמאה. Above the belt it could not, so she is טהורה. A sleeve is above the belt, but an arm can hang down, so it depends on whether that spot on the sleeve could reach across from בית התורפה.

keyTerms.meaning: The belt (the place where the garment is belted)
The sleeve (literally, 'the house of the hand')

steps.whyThisMatters: The sleeve shows that the test is not a fixed map of 'top half' and 'bottom half.' Even a part of the garment that is usually up high counts if it can actually reach the opening.

phrases.english: If she saw a stain on her robe:
from the belt and below, she is impure,
from the belt and above, she is pure.

phrases.aramaic: רָאֲתָה עַל בֵּית יָד שֶׁל חָלוּק,
phrases.english: If she saw it on the sleeve of the robe,

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַגִּיעַ כְּנֶגֶד בֵּית הַתּוּרְפָּה — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: if it reaches across from her vagina, she is impure,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the spot on the sleeve where the stain is. Could that part of the sleeve come down to the opening?

phrases.english: and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָאֲתָה עַל חֲלוּקָהּ מִן הֶחָגוּר וּלְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the test from her body to her clothing.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On the robe, below the belt makes her טמאה and above the belt she is טהורה. On the sleeve, she is טמאה only if that spot could reach across from בית התורפה.

steps.title: A robe used as a blanket at night, and a kerchief
steps.stepSummary: If she took off the robe and slept under it, a stain anywhere on it makes her טמאה, because the cloth moves around. The same rule applies to a פוליוס (kerchief).
steps.simpleTranslation: If she used to take it off and cover herself with it at night, wherever a stain is found on it, she is impure, because it moves around. And the same is true with a kerchief.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a case where the 'where is the stain' test no longer works: a cloth that shifts around while she sleeps. Here every spot counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The usual test asks whether a spot on the garment could reach the opening. A robe used as a blanket at night keeps moving, so any part of it may have touched that place. That is why a stain anywhere on it makes her טמאה, and the same goes for a פוליוס.
steps.whatToRemember: The whole משנה uses one test: could blood from בית התורפה have reached this spot? Near the opening, the heel and toe, the inner leg or foot, below the belt, or a sleeve that can reach: טמאה. Elsewhere: טהורה. A cloth that moves around at night counts everywhere, and the same goes for a פוליוס.

phrases.english: If she would take it off and cover herself with it at night,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the same robe from the last step, now used as a blanket.

phrases.aramaic: כָּל מָקוֹם שֶׁנִּמְצָא בּוֹ כֶּתֶם — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: wherever on it a stain is found, she is impure,
because it moves around,
and the same is true with a kerchief.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the robe from step 3 and shows when the 'above or below the belt' split no longer applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A garment she sleeps under shifts around, so a כתם anywhere on it makes her טמאה. The same applies to a פוליוס.

steps.title: שמואל: No sensation, no טומאה
steps.stepSummary: שמואל rules that a woman who checked the ground, sat on it, and then found blood there is טהורה, since the Torah says ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״, meaning she must feel it in her body.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: If a woman checked the ground and it was clean, then sat on it and found blood there, she is pure. The verse says 'in her flesh', which teaches that she is only impure if she feels the blood in her body.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a new rule from שמואל: finding blood is not enough to make a woman טמאה; she has to feel it come out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The blood very likely came from her, because the ground was clean before she sat down. Still, שמואל says she is טהורה, because the Torah ties נדה טומאה to a הרגשה, a physical sensation 'in her flesh'. Without that sensation, there is no טומאה מן התורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The plain ground (literally 'the ground of the world')
'In her flesh', the word from the פסוק about נדה
A physical sensation that blood is coming out

steps.whyThisMatters: The idea that a woman must feel the blood (הרגשה) for נדה טומאה מן התורה is a basic principle that the rest of the סוגיא tests.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Shmuel says:
If she examined the ground,
and she sat on it,
and found blood on it —
she is pure,
as it says, 'in her flesh' —
she is not impure unless she feels it in her flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא on the משנה about stains, adding a new rule about sensation.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found without a sensation does not make a woman טמאה מן התורה, learned from ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״.

steps.title: The word is already needed for another law
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ is already used to teach that blood still inside her body makes her טמאה just like blood that came outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he needs this word 'in her flesh' to teach that she becomes impure from blood inside her body just as from blood outside!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל: the word ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ is already 'taken' to teach a different law, so how can it also teach הרגשה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known teaching from ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״: blood that left the womb but is still inside her body already makes her טמאה, like blood outside. If the word is used up for that law, it seems it cannot be the source for שמואל's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (this word is needed for a different teaching)

phrases.english: But this 'in her flesh' — he needs it,
to teach that she becomes impure inside just as outside!
phrases.notes: Blood that left the womb but is still inside her body already counts.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the source שמואל used.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's use of ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ as the source for הרגשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word normally teaches one law; this word is already used for 'inside like outside'.

steps.title: The extra 'her' teaches sensation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the Torah could have written ״בְּבָשָׂר״; the extra 'her' in ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ teaches that she must feel it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the verse say 'in the flesh'. Why does it say 'in her flesh'? Learn from this: she is not impure unless she feels it in her flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by showing the word has an extra part: 'in the flesh' would be enough for the other law, so 'her flesh' adds something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The law of 'inside like outside' only needs the idea of 'in flesh'. The extra letter ה ('her') is not needed for that, so it is free to teach that the sensation must be felt in her own body.
steps.whatToRemember: ״בְּבָשָׂר״ would teach 'inside like outside'; the extra 'her' in ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ teaches הרגשה.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse say 'in the flesh',
why 'in her flesh'?
Learn from it: not unless she feels it in her flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra word in the פסוק (ייתור לשון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ is fully used up for 'inside like outside'.
steps.terutzMaskana: ''בְּבָשָׂר'' would teach 'inside like outside'; the extra 'her' teaches הרגשה.

steps.title: Still another law from the same word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again: ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ is also needed to teach that blood found in a שפיר or a חתיכה does not make her טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But he still needs 'in her flesh' to teach: not through a gestational sac, and not through a piece of tissue!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes again: even the full word ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ ('her' included) seems needed for yet another law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a teaching that blood must touch her own flesh; if it came out wrapped inside a שפיר or a חתיכה, she is not טמאה. That law seems to need the word 'her flesh', so again the word looks used up.

keyTerms.meaning: A piece of tissue that came out of her

phrases.english: And still, he needs 'in her flesh',
and not in a gestational sac, and not in a piece of tissue!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge after the answer in step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the extra 'her' in ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ for הרגשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even 'her flesh' is needed to exclude blood in a שפיר or חתיכה, so it is not free for הרגשה.

steps.title: Learn both laws from the word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ teaches both laws at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers simply: the word ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ teaches both the rule about שפיר and חתיכה and שמואל's rule about הרגשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both laws come from the same plain meaning: the blood must be in contact with, and felt in, her own flesh. So one word can carry both teachings, and שמואל's source stands.
steps.whatToRemember: ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ teaches 'inside like outside' (from 'flesh'), and both 'not in a שפיר or חתיכה' and שמואל's הרגשה rule (from 'her flesh').

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 8 and closes the source discussion.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each law needs its own separate word.
steps.terutzMaskana: ''בִּבְשָׂרָהּ'' teaches both the שפיר/חתיכה law and הרגשה.

steps.title: Bringing a משנה about blood while urinating
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה: a woman who sees blood while urinating is טמאה if standing and טהורה if sitting, according to רבי מאיר. This is a test of שמואל's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: A woman who is urinating and sees blood — רבי מאיר says: if she is standing, she is impure; if she is sitting, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move: it quotes a משנה to test שמואל's rule. The actual question about this משנה comes right after.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר splits the case: standing is טמאה, sitting is טהורה. The next step uses that split to argue that this must be a case with no sensation at all, and yet standing is still טמאה, which would go against שמואל.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא has not asked its question yet. This line only quotes the משנה; the challenge to שמואל comes next.

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה צְרָכֶיהָ,
phrases.english: Come and hear: A woman who is urinating,
and she saw blood.
Rabbi Meir says:
If she is standing — she is impure,
and if she is sitting — she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאִשָּׁה שֶׁהִיא עוֹשָׂה צְרָכֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the source of שמואל's rule is secured, the גמרא tests the rule itself against a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that she is only טמאה with a sensation of blood
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she had felt the blood, sitting should also be טמאה. So the case must be one with no sensation, yet standing is ruled טמאה, which seems to show טומאה without הרגשה.

steps.title: The urination case must be one where she felt nothing
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא analyzes the urination משנה. If she felt the blood, why is she טהורה when sitting? So she must not have felt it, and yet standing makes her טמאה. That goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she felt it, why is she pure when sitting? So it must be a case where she did not feel it. And still the משנה teaches that when standing she is impure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה from step 10 is a problem for שמואל. It shows that the case must be one where she felt nothing, yet she can still be טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא tries both options. If she felt the blood, שמואל would make her טמאה even when sitting, but the משנה says she is טהורה. So the משנה must be talking about no feeling at all, and then 'standing is טמאה' means a woman can be טמאה without הרגשה. That contradicts שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What exactly are the circumstances?
She felt it (the sensation of blood leaving her body)
Rather, is it not that…? (pushes toward the only remaining option)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If she felt it,
then when sitting, why is she pure?
Rather, is it not a case where she did not feel it?
And yet it teaches: standing, she is impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 10 by showing how the משנה contradicts שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that she is טמאה only if she feels it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a no-feeling case fits the משנה's 'sitting is טהורה', yet standing makes her טמאה without any feeling.

steps.title: She did feel it, but the feeling may have been the urine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה really is a case where she felt something. That feeling could be from the urine. When standing, the urine flows back to the מקור and brings blood out, so she is טמאה. When sitting, she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, she felt it. But we can say it was the feeling of urine. When standing, the urine went back to the source and brought out blood. When sitting, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל. It says the משנה is a case where she did feel something, and it explains why sitting is still טהורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since she was urinating, her feeling can be blamed on the urine instead of the blood. When standing, the urine flows back into the מקור and pulls real blood out from there, so she is טמאה. When sitting, that does not happen, so we say the feeling was just the urine and she stays טהורה. שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, in truth (begins an answer that keeps the original reading)
The source, the uterus, where impure blood comes from

steps.confusionAlert: Sitting is not טהורה because she felt nothing. She did feel something, but we blame the feeling on the urine.

phrases.english: Really, it is a case where she felt it,
but say: "it was the feeling of urine."
Standing: the urine went back to the source
and brought out blood,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets and some have the one in square brackets. Both mean 'brought'.

phrases.english: and sitting: she is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: there was a feeling, but it can be blamed on the urine
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must be a no-feeling case, which goes against שמואל.
steps.terutzMaskana: There was a feeling. Standing: urine brings blood from the מקור, so she is טמאה. Sitting: the feeling is blamed on the urine, so she is טהורה.

steps.title: A new source: a בדיקה cloth found under the pillow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings another משנה. If a בדיקה cloth was under the pillow and blood is found on it, a round stain is טהור and a stretched-out stain is טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a בדיקה cloth that was placed under the pillow, and blood was found on it. If the stain is round, it is pure. If it is stretched out, it is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second משנה to test שמואל again. This step only quotes the source. The next step explains the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A round stain probably came from something like a crushed bug, so it is טהור. A stretched-out stain looks like it was wiped during a בדיקה, so it is טמא. The question coming next is whether she felt anything in this case.

keyTerms.meaning: A בדיקה cloth (used to check for blood)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
A בדיקה cloth that was placed under the pillow,
and blood was found on it:
if it is round, it is pure,
and if it is stretched out, it is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: עֵד שֶׁהָיָה נָתוּן תַּחַת הַכַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The first challenge was answered, so the גמרא brings a new source against שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that she is טמאה only if she feels it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה makes a stretched-out stain טמא with no mention of any feeling.

steps.title: The pillow-cloth case must be one where she felt nothing
steps.stepSummary: If she felt it, why would a round stain be טהור? So she must not have felt it, and yet a stretched-out stain is טמא. That goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she felt it, why is a round stain pure? So it must be a case where she did not feel it. And still the משנה teaches that a stretched-out stain is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the same reasoning as in step 11 on the new משנה. It shows that a stretched-out stain makes her טמאה even though she felt nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she had felt blood, there would be no reason to call a round stain טהור. So the משנה must be talking about no feeling. Then 'stretched out is טמא' means she becomes טמאה without הרגשה, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Where she did not feel it

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא uses the same pattern twice: 'If she felt it, the טהור ruling makes no sense, so she must not have felt it, and yet the משנה rules טמא.' The first time it was answered. The next step answers this second challenge.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If she felt it,
why is a round stain pure?
Rather, is it not a case where she did not feel it?
And yet it teaches: a stretched-out stain is impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge from step 13, using the same reasoning as step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that she is טמאה only if she feels it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only a no-feeling case explains why a round stain is טהור, yet a stretched-out stain is still טמא.

steps.title: She felt it, but the feeling may have come from the cloth
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the pillow-cloth משנה is a case where she did feel something. Since the feeling could have come from the בדיקה cloth, the shape of the stain decides: stretched-out is from her body, round is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really she did feel something. But we can say that what she felt was just the cloth. So if the stain is stretched out, it surely came from her body. If it is round, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 14 by saying the משנה really is a case where she felt something.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that if she felt something, even a round stain would be טמא. The answer is that her feeling is not clear proof, because she may have felt the בדיקה cloth itself. So the stain's shape decides: a stretched-out stain matches blood wiped from her body, while a round stain does not, so it stays טהור. שמואל's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: The feeling caused by the examination cloth itself
Really, actually (used to keep the original reading of a case)

steps.whyThisMatters: This repeats the pattern from Step 12, and the next answer uses it again: she felt something, but the feeling might have had another cause.

phrases.english: No, really it is a case where she felt it,
but one could say, "It was the feeling of the cloth,"
phrases.notes: The עֵד here is the בדיקה cloth she checked herself with, so what she felt might just have been the cloth.

phrases.english: if stretched out, it surely came from her body;
if round, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: she felt something, but the feeling has another possible cause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must mean she felt nothing, since otherwise a round stain would be טמא
steps.terutzMaskana: She felt something, but it may have been the cloth, so the shape of the stain decides

steps.title: A new משנה: blood found on cloths after relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a משנה about blood found on the husband's or wife's cloth after relations, and when they must bring a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: If blood is found on his cloth, they are טמאים and must bring a קרבן. If it is found on her cloth right away, they are טמאים and must bring a קרבן. If it is found on her cloth after some time, they are טמאים because of doubt, and do not bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה as another test of שמואל's rule. This step only quotes the source; the next step will explain the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on his cloth, or on hers right away, shows she was a נדה during relations, so they need a חטאת. Blood found on hers only later might have come after relations, so it is only a doubt and there is no קרבן. The גמרא will now ask whether this case involves her feeling anything.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, a חַטָּאת brought for doing by mistake an act that carries כָּרֵת
Right away, at that very time

phrases.english: Come and hear:
If blood was found on his cloth, they are impure,
phrases.notes: "His" means the cloth the husband checks himself with after relations.

phrases.english: and they must bring an offering.
If found on hers right away, they are impure,
and they must bring an offering.
If found on hers after some time,
they are impure because of doubt, and exempt from the offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the pillow-cloth challenge is answered, a new source is brought to test שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that she is טמאה only with a הרגשה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: the source will be shown to make her טמאה without a feeling

steps.title: Proving the משנה is a case where she felt nothing
steps.stepSummary: If she felt something, blood found later should also bring a קרבן. Since it does not, she must not have felt anything, yet blood found right away makes them טמאים, which goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If she felt it, why are they exempt from the קרבן when the blood is found later? It must be that she did not feel it. And yet the משנה says that blood found on her cloth right away makes them טמאים and they must bring a קרבן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the משנה from Step 16 seems to go against שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she had felt blood come out during relations, we would know when it came, and even a later find would require a קרבן. Since a later find is only a doubt, the משנה must be talking about no feeling at all. But then the right-away case makes her טמאה without a feeling, which goes against שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How do we picture it?
Rather, is it not that...? (leading to a forced reading)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If she felt it,

phrases.aramaic: לְאַחַר זְמַן אַמַּאי פְּטוּרִין מִן הַקׇּרְבָּן?
phrases.english: then after some time, why are they exempt from the offering?
Rather, is it not that she did not feel it?
And yet it teaches: if found on hers right away,
they are impure and must bring an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Works out the challenge from the משנה quoted in Step 16
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The exemption in the later case shows there was no feeling, yet the right-away case is fully טמא and needs a קרבן

steps.title: She felt it, but it may have been the feeling of relations
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that she did feel something, but the feeling could have come from the relations themselves, so a later find stays only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Really she felt something. But we can say it was the feeling of the relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 17 with the same idea as Step 15: there was a feeling, but it may have had another cause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: She felt something, so the right-away case fits שמואל. But since relations were going on, her feeling may have come from that and not from blood. So blood found later is not clearly tied to that moment, and they are exempt from the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: A polite word for the male organ

phrases.english: No, really it is a case where she felt it,
but one could say it was the feeling of relations.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, לְעוֹלָם דְּאַרְגִּישָׁה, וְאֵימָא הַרְגָּשַׁת שַׁמָּשׁ הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: she felt something, but the feeling may have another cause
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The exemption shows she felt nothing at all
steps.terutzMaskana: She felt something, which fits שמואל, but it may have been from relations, so a later find stays a doubt
steps.whatToRemember: Three times now the גמרא saves שמואל the same way: she did feel something, but the feeling could be explained by something else (the urine, the cloth, or relations).

steps.title: A ברייתא about three kinds of doubt with a woman
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: a doubtful stain on her body is טמא, on her garment is טהור, and for her touching and moving things we follow the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: You find three doubts with a woman. On her body, if it is unclear whether it is טמא or טהור, it is טמא. On her garment, if unclear, it is טהור. And for things she touched or moved, follow the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as a new test of שמואל. This step only quotes the source and sets up the next challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists three doubtful cases with three different results. A doubtful stain on her body is treated as טמא, which may seem to make her טמאה without any feeling. The גמרא will look into this next.

keyTerms.meaning: Things she touched and things she moved

phrases.english: Come and hear:
You are found to say
there are three doubts with a woman:

phrases.aramaic: עַל בְּשָׂרָה, סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר — טָמֵא.
phrases.english: on her body, unclear if impure or pure — impure.

phrases.aramaic: עַל חֲלוּקָהּ, סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר — טָהוֹר.
phrases.english: On her garment, unclear if impure or pure — pure.
And with things she touched and moved,
follow the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: נִמְצֵאתָ אַתָּה אוֹמֵר שְׁלֹשָׁה סְפֵקוֹת בָּאִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the second challenge is answered, a third source is brought
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup: a doubtful stain on her body is ruled טמא, apparently without a feeling

steps.title: Does 'follow the majority' mean impure even without a feeling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'follow the majority' as: if most of her days she is טמאה, she is טמאה now even without a feeling. That goes against שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'follow the majority' mean? Doesn't it mean that if most of her days are impure, she is impure, even though she felt nothing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the words 'follow the majority' from the ברייתא in a way that attacks שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not mention a feeling at all. If the majority rule is about how many of her days are impure, then she becomes טמאה even with no feeling. That goes against שמואל, who needs a הרגשה.

phrases.english: What does 'follow the majority' mean?
phrases.notes: These words come from the ברייתא in Step 19, about the things she touches and moves.

phrases.english: Doesn't it mean: if most of her days are impure
she is impure,
even though she did not feel anything?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the ברייתא quoted in Step 19
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a woman is טמאה only if she felt something
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The majority rule makes her טמאה based on how many of her days are impure, with no mention of a feeling.

steps.title: The majority means she usually sees with a feeling
steps.stepSummary: No. The majority means that most times she sees blood, she feels it. So we assume she felt it this time too but did not notice.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. If most of her days she sees blood with a feeling, she is impure, because we can say she did feel it but did not pay attention.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends שמואל by reading 'majority' in a different way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority is not about impure days. It is about her usual pattern of sensing when she bleeds. So she is treated as having felt it this time too, and שמואל's need for a הרגשה still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was not on her mind; she did not notice

phrases.english: No,
if on most of her days she sees blood with a feeling
she is impure,
because we say she felt it, but did not pay attention.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִם רוֹב יָמֶיהָ בְּהַרְגָּשָׁה חָזְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 20
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Majority meant most of her days are impure, so no feeling is needed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Majority means she usually feels when she bleeds, so we assume a feeling she missed.
steps.whatToRemember: 'Follow the majority' here means her usual pattern of bleeding with a feeling, so שמואל's rule still holds.

steps.title: Quoting the body-versus-garment line of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes another line from the same ברייתא: a doubtful stain on her body is טמא, and on her garment it is טהור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: on her flesh, if it is unclear whether it is impure or pure, it is impure. On her robe, if it is unclear, it is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look at another line of the ברייתא. It is setting up a question about it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cases are placed side by side, which suggests the stain was in the same spot on her in both. That is what makes the next question possible: how can the same spot give two different rulings?

keyTerms.meaning: Unclear whether it is impure or pure

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: This just means: the ברייתא we quoted earlier said.

phrases.aramaic: עַל בְּשָׂרָה סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר
phrases.english: On her flesh, unclear whether impure or pure
it is impure;

phrases.aramaic: עַל חֲלוּקָהּ סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר
phrases.english: on her robe, unclear whether impure or pure
it is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: עַל בְּשָׂרָה סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שמואל question for now and re-quotes another clause of the ברייתא from Step 19 to look at it closely
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A doubtful stain on her body is טמא, and on her garment it is טהור.

steps.title: Where was the stain: below the belt or above it?
steps.stepSummary: If the stain was below the belt, the garment should be טמא. If it was above the belt, the body should be טהור. Either way, the ברייתא clashes with a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If it was from the belt and below, why is it pure on her robe? We learned that from the belt and below it is impure! And if it was from the belt and above, why is it impure on her body? We learned that blood on her body not near the private area is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where on her the stain was found, and shows that both choices run into trouble.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says a garment stain below the belt is טמא, so the 'garment is טהור' ruling cannot be about below the belt. The same משנה also says a body stain away from the private area is טהור, so the 'body is טמא' ruling cannot be about above the belt. No single spot seems to fit both rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the circumstances?
The private area (where blood comes out)

phrases.english: What is the case?
If it was from the belt and below,
why is it pure on her robe?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא תְנַן: מִן הֶחָגוּר וּלְמַטָּה טָמֵא!
phrases.english: But we learned: from the belt and below, it is impure!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה about a stain found on her garment.

phrases.english: And if it was from the belt and above,
why is it impure on her flesh?
But we learned: if she saw blood on her flesh
not near the private area, she is pure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא clause quoted in Step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a doubtful stain is טמא on her body but טהור on her garment
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-sided dilemma. Below the belt clashes with the משנה that a garment stain there is טמא. Above the belt clashes with the משנה that a body stain away from the private area is טהור.
steps.confusionAlert: The two rulings in the ברייתא are about the SAME spot on her. The question is not 'body versus garment' in general. It is that no one spot fits both rulings.

steps.title: First answer: below the belt, after a butchers' market
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers two ways to explain the ברייתא. The first: the stain was below the belt, but she had walked through a butchers' market.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say it was below the belt, or you can say it was above the belt. If below the belt: she walked through a butchers' market. A stain on her body must come from her, because blood from outside would have landed on her garment. A stain on her garment must come from outside, because blood from her body would have been found on her skin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 23 by saying there are two possible cases. This step explains the first one: below the belt, in a butchers' market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a stain below the belt on the garment is טמא. Here she walked past butchers, so outside blood was around, and a stain only on the garment is blamed on the butchers. A stain on her skin but not on the garment over it cannot be from outside, so it is from her body.

keyTerms.meaning: a butchers' market, where blood from animals is everywhere
from the outside world, from some other source

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two places. Blood from outside hits the garment first. Blood from her body touches her skin first. That is the whole logic of this step.

phrases.english: If you want, say: from the belt and below,
and if you want, say: from the belt and above.
If you want, say from the belt and below,
for example, where she passed through a butchers' market.
If it is on her flesh, it came from her body,
because if it came from outside,
it should have been found on her garment.
If it is on her garment, it came from outside,
because if it came from her body,
it should have been found on her flesh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma from step 23 by naming a special case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ברייתא to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A stain below the belt on the garment should be טמא, so the ברייתא seemed to clash with the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: She walked through a butchers' market, so a stain only on the garment can be blamed on outside blood.

steps.title: Second answer: above the belt, after she jumped
steps.stepSummary: The other way to explain the ברייתא: the stain was above the belt, but she jumped, so blood from her body could reach that high.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say it was above the belt, for example when she jumped. A stain on her flesh surely came from her body, because outside blood would have been on her garment. A stain on her garment came from outside, because blood from her body would have been on her flesh.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second case: above the belt, when she jumped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a stain above the belt on her body is טהור, because her own blood would not get up there. Once she jumped, her blood could reach higher. So a stain on her skin is treated as hers, and the ברייתא no longer clashes with the משנה.

phrases.english: And if you want, say: from the belt and above,
for example, where she jumped.
If it is on her flesh, it surely came from her body,
because if it came from outside,
it should have been found on her garment.
If it is on her garment, it came from outside,
because if it came from her body,
it should have been found on her flesh.

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא fits the משנה either way: below the belt after a butchers' market, or above the belt after she jumped.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second way to answer the same question from step 23.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A stain above the belt on the body should be טהור.
steps.terutzMaskana: She jumped, so her blood could reach above the belt, and a stain on her flesh is treated as hers.

steps.title: The ברייתא calls her טמאה without a feeling
steps.stepSummary: Now that the ברייתא is explained, the גמרא uses it against שמואל: a doubtful stain on her flesh is טמא even though she felt nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: on her flesh, if it is unclear whether it is טמא or טהור, it is טמא, even though she did not feel anything.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main question and challenges שמואל again from the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Whatever case the ברייתא is talking about, it still says a stain on her flesh makes her טמאה. A stain means she did not feel the blood come out. That goes against שמואל, who says she is only טמאה if she felt it.

keyTerms.meaning: she felt it, meaning she sensed the blood leaving her body

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: עַל בְּשָׂרָהּ סָפֵק טָמֵא סָפֵק טָהוֹר טָמֵא,
phrases.english: on her flesh, unsure if impure or pure, it is impure,
even though she did not feel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the side question about the ברייתא and goes back to challenging שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's rule that a woman is only טמאה if she felt the blood.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא calls a stain on her flesh טמא, and a stain comes without any feeling.

steps.title: A משנה also says a stain makes her טמאה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second source: the משנה says a woman who finds a stain on her flesh near the private area is טמאה, even without a feeling.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned in a משנה: a woman who sees a stain on her flesh across from the private area is טמאה, even though she did not feel it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא strengthens its challenge against שמואל with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same kind of proof as before, but from a משנה, which carries even more weight. A stain, found by seeing and not by feeling, still makes her טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: a stain of blood found on the body or clothing

phrases.english: And furthermore, we learned:
a woman who sees a stain on her flesh
across from the private area is impure,
even though she did not feel it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source to the challenge in step 26.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה calls her טמאה from a stain alone, without any feeling.

steps.title: שמואל agrees she is טמאה
steps.stepSummary: רב ירמיה מדפתי answers that שמואל himself agrees she is טמאה in these stain cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ירמיה from Difti said: שמואל agrees that she is טמאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ירמיה defends שמואל by saying שמואל does not argue on these sources. The statement goes on past this point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sources do not prove שמואל wrong, because he admits she is טמאה here. The end of רב ירמיה's sentence, on the next amud, explains that this agreement is only מדרבנן. שמואל's need for a feeling is a rule מן התורה, while stain cases make her טמאה by rabbinic law.
steps.whyThisMatters: Stain cases are treated as their own category, so שמואל's rule about feeling stays in place even though a stain can still make her טמאה.

phrases.english: Rav Yirmeya of Difti said:
Shmuel agrees that she is impure

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יִרְמְיָה מִדִּפְתִּי מוֹדֶה שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges of steps 26 and 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Concession: שמואל agrees with the ruling, so there is no clash.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The sources seemed to prove that שמואל was wrong.
steps.terutzMaskana: שמואל agrees she is טמאה in these stain cases, and the next words give the reason.
